gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on YesWelder's own store the TIG-200P ACDC PRO with its foot pedal ($599.15) costs $49.85 less than the machine alone ($649.00), so the pedal-equipped AC/DC kit for aluminum costs $599.15, not the $649 + pedal that ChatGPT and homewelder.com imply.
standout_why: Against the cited homewelder.com/best-tig-welder-for-beginners (2026-10-11): it lists the TIG-200P ACDC PRO at $649 with 'pedal sold separately' and cannot give an all-in price with the pedal. It also has no 110 V duty-cycle figures for this model, only the 200 A at 30% rating on 220 V. Against the cited woodworking-projects.com/hobby-tig-welder (updated 2026-10-20): it gives price ranges only, no pedal price, no 120 V AC amps for any model, and no all-in price. ChatGPT's answer itself says 'Foot pedal may cost extra' at $649.00. None of these pages show the pedal bundle priced below the bare machine.
decides: Changes how the YesWelder pick should be shown. Buy the '& Foot Pedal' option at $599.15, never the $649 bare machine. That puts a pedal-equipped AC/DC HF-start machine about $70 below the AHP 203Xi's quoted ~$670, though that figure comes from a reviewer page and was not checked on a store today. For 120 V-only beginners it also confirms the machine can run continuously at 108 A on a 110 V outlet. The pick for steel plus aluminum on a budget is therefore the YesWelder pedal bundle, unless PrimeWeld's pedal-included price, which I could not source today, comes in under that.

findings.note: Maker duty cycle TIG 220 V: 30% at 200 A, 100% at 110 A. 0.30 x 10 = 3.0 min. The continuous current on 220 V (110 A) is about the same as on 110 V (108 A).
